title: WM8994 will not do analog output to Green Jack if using SAI frequency less than 16kHz
body:
`SAI` peripheral passes `SAI1_MCLKA` (PG7 on MB1248 p. 2) down to the `WM8994` at GPIO `MCLK1` which, by default, acts as the system clock for that codec. For the chip to work, a minimum frequency of $4.096MHz$ (WM8994_Rev4.6 p. 191) is required. `SAI1_MCLKA` will only reach that threshold if $F_{MCLK\_A} \ge 16kHz$, as indicated by $F_{MCLK\_x} = 256 * F_{FS\_x}$ (RM0399 p. 2402).

If $F_{FS\_x} \lt 16kHz$ then $F_{MCLK\_x} \lt 4.096 MHz$ and `WM8994` will not work as expected without going too much into the internals.

comments.author: DannyCato
comments.body:
To solve this, the plan for my project was for `MCLK1` to be passed in as the input sample rate for `Audio Interface 1 (AIF1)`. The `SYSCLK` would be multiplexed to use `AIF2`'s Clock which would again be multiplexed to use `FLL1` present on the `WM8994` (diagram on WM8994_Rev4.6 p.192). An idea for implementation is that `FLL1` over `AIF2` could be the `WM8994`'s system clock regardless of the frequency being used (I am not familiar with any boards that might use `AIF2`). As long as `SYSCLK` stays within $4.096-12.5MHz$ then things should run normally though (p.191).

I would like to pull this down and make the change, but it seems like a little bit too big of an architectural change for someone not affiliated.

comments.author: ASAHSTM
comments.body:
Hello @DannyCato,

Thank you for your report.
If I understand you correctly, you need to configure the audio sample rate below 16 kHz. With the current SAI configuration (MCLK = 256 × FS), this would put the WM8994 outside its clock specification.

Could you please clarify why you need an audio frequency below 16 kHz? Is there a specific application requirement or constraint behind this choice?

Regarding your proposed solution (reorganizing the clocking scheme using SYSCLK / FLL1 / AIF1 / AIF2), this kind of architectural change is difficult to implement on our current HW/SW setup and would require a major rework. For this platform, we can support sample rates that keep the WM8994 system clock within its specified range (FS ≥ 16 kHz with the existing MCLK configuration).

With Regards

comments.author: DannyCato
ASAHSTM
comments.body:
Hello @DannyCato,

Thank you for the additional clarification. It is a very interesting use‑case.

From the WM8994 side, the behavior you observe is unfortunately expected with the current clocking scheme used on MB1248. So, the limitation is not in the STM32 SAI peripheral itself but in the way the codec system clock is derived on this platform. 
Regarding your proposal, implementing this change on the current MB1248 + BSP would require a significant hardware / BSP re‑architecture (clock tree, routing, initialization code, validation) and would impact all existing examples and applications that rely on the current audio clock configuration.

For these reasons, we are not planning to introduce such a change in the official BSP for this board.

So, please allow me to close this issue.

With Regards,

title: Hardcoded default SAI slot
body:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h747i-disco-bsp/blob/bb81c6532fcc301fc760a98f8a42acede46bea83/stm32h747i_discovery_audio.c#L282

SAI active slot is set appropriately for headphone output, regardless of audioinit device selection. I was not able to get output on the speaker ports without changing this to the appropriate codec slot for speaker/spk+hp.

Any reason this shouldn't be chosen automatically based on AudioInit->Device ..?

Thank you.

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @pepfof,

Thank you for the report.

In fact, there is two functions, one for the BSP_AUDIO_OUT_Init() and the other for BSP_AUDIO_IN_Init(), also there is a list of SAI Slot that must be activated for type of audio stream, below an extract from the header file:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h747i-disco-bsp/blob/bb81c6532fcc301fc760a98f8a42acede46bea83/stm32h747i_discovery_audio.h#L185-L199

In addition, there is an example BSP under `\Projects\STM32H747I-DISCO\Examples\BSP\EWARM` that contain 2 Demos, `AudioPlay_demo and AudioRecord_demo` for this board, but unavailable on this repository as mentioned on the readme file, because they `are subject to some restrictive license terms requiring the user's approval via a "click thru" procedure.`

However, you can download the [package](https://www.st.com/en/embedded-software/stm32cubeh7.html#get-software), and you can check it for more details.

I hope this may help you.

With regards,

comments.author: pepfof
comments.body:
Hi @KRASTM,

Yes, thank you for this note, but my question/suggestion was - why is CODEC_AUDIOFRAME_SLOT_02 hardcoded in BSP_AUDIO_OUT(IN)_Init? 

We pass the device(s) we want to activate through the init struct to these functions, shouldn't they infer from this the codec slot to use? 

If this is done, it would be sufficient to only change the device in the init structure, and you wouldn't have to change BSP code in multiple places just to change the audio device... 

Besides, the way the current code is written doesn't allow the user to use different devices subsequently (without not-insignificantly rewriting bsp code)

Regards

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @pepfof,

I shared your idea with our team, apparently it is related to a specific configuration and a choice from the developer, that's why the slot is hardcoded in the 2 functions.

I concur with your recommendation, but unfortunately, there is no plan to update BSP driver in the short term. I will keep you informed if there are any updates. Please allow me to close this issue.

Thank you in advance for your comprehension.

With regards.

title: Wrong default for `LCD_LAYER_0_ADDRESS` and `LCD_LAYER_1_ADDRESS`
body:
**Describe the bug (skip if none)**

The defaults for `LCD_LAYER_0_ADDRESS` and `LCD_LAYER_1_ADDRESS` in `stm32h747i_discovery_conf_template.h` are 

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h747i-disco-bsp/blob/bb81c6532fcc301fc760a98f8a42acede46bea83/stm32h747i_discovery_conf_template.h#L39

`0xC0000000U` and `0xC0200000U`. That's by default not a mapped memory region.

The intention was most likely to default to the SDRAM region that's at `0xD0000000` as per https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h747i-disco-bsp/blob/bb81c6532fcc301fc760a98f8a42acede46bea83/stm32h747i_discovery_sdram.h#L63

This also matches RM0433 (2.3.2).

The effect of these (IMO wrong) defaults is that out of the box the default layer initialised by `BSP_LCD_Init`/`BSP_LCD_InitEx` is at the wrong address and any layer access results in a memory fault.

I'd be happy to make a PR to correct these, but I wanted to check first that I'm not missing anything :)

comments.author: ASEHSTM
comments.body:
Hello @tronical,

Thank you for your report. We have not encountered any issues with these definitions in our examples. According to the reference manual, the 0xC0000000 region (SDRAM Bank 1) is valid for use.
Could you please specify if you detected a problem with these LCD layer definitions during execution, or if it was identified through a visual check?

Thank you in advance for your cooperation.

With Regards.

comments.author: tronical
comments.body:
Hi,

I encountered this problem during execution. The symptom is a memory fault.

To reproduce: generate a new template with CubeMX for this board, add the BSP, call the LCD init functions, then try to write to the layer address. It crashes.

While the current value may be valid _if_ something is mapped there, the BSP in this report defaults to mapping the SD-RAM to 0xD.

Also note how _all_ examples that use the lcd functions of this BSP also end up with 0xD.

comments.author: ASEHSTM
comments.body:
Hello @tronical,

Thank you for bringing this to our attention. You are right, this issue will be fixed soon.
ST Internal Reference: 187832

With Regards,

title: Unable to configure I2C4 bus from IOC editor, MX_I2C4_Init() name conflict.
body:
Board: STM32H747I-DISCO
 IDE: STM32CubeIDE 1.9.0

**PROBLEM:**

Configuring I2C4 in IOC editor generates the code that results in name conflict in function:
```c
static void MX_I2C4_Init(void);
```

That collides with BSP bus driver function:
```c
HAL_StatusTypeDef MX_I2C4_Init(I2C_HandleTypeDef *phi2c, uint32_t timing);
```

The project does not compile.

**WORKAROUND:**

Change the function signature:
```c
HAL_StatusTypeDef MX_I2C4_Init(I2C_HandleTypeDef *phi2c, uint32_t timing);
```
to
```c
HAL_StatusTypeDef _MX_I2C4_Init(I2C_HandleTypeDef *phi2c, uint32_t timing);
```

Update references in stm32h737i_discovery_bus.c file.

After applying the workaround above the project compiles and works properly.
